div.head: V Atr 28
div.ab: ⁊ gyf hwa butan leafe of fyrde gewende, þe se cyning sylf on sy, plihte him sylfum ⁊ ealre his are.
⁊ gif hwa butan leafe of fyrde gewende, þe se cyning sylf on sy, plihte him sylfum oððe wergylde.
And gif hwa buton leafe of firde gewænde, þe se cyninge silf on sy, plihte him silfum oððe wergilde.
And gif hwa buton leafe of firde gewænde þe se cyningc silf on sy, plihte him silfum oððe wergilde.
And gyf hwa butan leafe of fyrde gewende þe se cyning sylf on sy, plihte him sylfum and ealre his are.
Und wenn jemand ohne Erlaubniss von der Landwehr, bei der der König selbst ist, fortgeht, bringe er seinem Leben und seiner Besitzstellung (oder seinem Wergeld G2 D) Verwirkungsgefahr.
And if anyone leaves the army without permission when the king himself is with it, let him put at risk his life and his whole property (or his wergild, G2 D).
And if anyone deserts an army which is under the personal command of the king, it shall be at the risk of [losing] his life or his wergeld.
And if anyone deserts without leave from an army which the king himself is with, it is to be at the peril of his life and all his property.
And if anyone deserts an army led by the king himself, he shall risk forfeiture of his life and all his property.

div.note: In VI Atr 35, ‘his are’ without danger to life; II Cn 77 threatens property and life. Perhaps ‘oððe wergilde’ stood in the margin of the archetype (Liebermann).
and ealre his are: oððe wergylde G2D
all his property: Cambridge, Corpus Christi College MS 201 replaces this phrase with “or his wergild.”

note.seg: his are ohne Lebensgefahr VI Atr. 35; Habe und Leben bedroht II Cnut 77; vielleicht am Rande des Archetyps stand oððe wergilde
his are without danger to life VI Atr. 35; property and life threatened II Cnut 77; perhaps oððe wergilde stood in the margin of the archetype

plihtan (s. d. Wb) verbindet sich stets mit Leben oder Gesamthabe: him sylfum, æhtum, are. Schon darum scheint ‘oder Wergeld’ nicht ursprünglich. Vermutlich will ein Randglossator des Archetyps die Todesstrafe (s. d. Gl 7) mildern (wie D in 29⁴) und setzt alternativ daneben Wergeld (s. d. Gl 29. 30a), das öfter dafür eintritt; zugleich lässt er are ‘Grundbesitz (s. d. Gl 1. 9. 13) samt daran hängendem Rang’ fort, was VI Atr 35, von V abweichend, allein ohne Todesdrohung, beibehält

plihtan (see that word in Wb) is always combined with life or entire property: him sylfum, æhtum, are. For that reason alone ‘or wergild’ seems not to be original. Presumably a marginal glossator of the archetype wishes to mitigate the death penalty (see that word in Gl 7) (as D does in 29⁴) and sets beside it, as an alternative, wergild (see that word in Gl 29. 30a), which often takes its place; at the same time he omits are ‘landed property (see that word in Gl 1. 9. 13) together with the rank attaching to it’, which VI Atr 35, departing from V, retains on its own, without the threat of death

Lit. ‘in which the king himself is present.’
The payment of wergeld is frequently found in the Laws as the alternative to the death penalty, cf. Wi. 26; In. 12; 15; Af. 7, 1; VI As. 1, 4. G adds ‘and all his property.’
